title: Sean Cairncross out, Kirsten A. Davies in as White House national cyber director: source
summary: Sean Cairncross is out as the White House's national cyber director, a source close to the White House told CBC News on Thursday.

image.caption: Sean Cairncross, seen attending a conference in Menlo Park, Calif., earlier this week, is out as the White House national cyber director. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Sean Cairncross is out as the White House's national cyber director, a source close to the White House told CBC News on Thursday.
Shake-up follows recent series of high-profile tech problems state-side
He's being replaced, in an acting capacity, by Kirsten A. Davies, who has been serving as the chief information officer at the U.S. Department of War.
CBC News is not identifying the source, who provided the information on condition they not be named.

The shake-up follows a series of high-profile tech problems state-side in recent days — including an apparent IT incident that caused a nation-wide ground stop of flights in the U.S. last week, and headline-grabbing service outages involving Microsoft products and bank transactions. The U.S. National Security Agency also saw its classified internal communications go offline.
The national cyber director leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which was created in 2021.
U.S. President Donald Trump is said to be supportive of the change, which the administration views as strengthening its cybersecurity team.

An existing biography for Davies on the Department of War's website cites her near two decades of prior "executive leadership experience at the intersection of cybersecurity, enterprise technology, and large-scale organizational transformation," before joining the government.

Cairncross was confirmed by the U.S. Senate for the role in August 2025. A White House statement at that time had touted his "extensive leadership experience," prior to taking the cyber director role.
